title: Control cartography — scratch journal (Ina)
content:
Purpose:
Quick, portable notebook for control cartography — sketching mappings between our operational controls and SOC2 criteria, surfacing gaps and cheap experiments to raise confidence. Not polished; notes to self and actions at bottom.

High-level framing:
- Cartography metaphor: draw the map (what controls exist), mark terrain (systems + owners), then annotate risk paths (how a threat flows).
- Focus first on the highest-impact surfaces: API auth, model artifact provenance, build/deploy pipeline, logging/retention, and access to production data.

Preliminary control map (text table):
1) Control: API token issuance + rotation | SOC2: CC6 (access control) | Owner: infra/auth team | Evidence: auth-service/rotations/README + k8s secret rotation job | Confidence: medium | Note: rotation window currently 90 days — consider reducing for service keys

2) Control: Model artifact signing & provenance | SOC2: CC4/CC6 | Owner: applied-ml | Evidence: s3://model-artifacts/sha-manifest + internal PRs | Confidence: low | Note: ad-hoc today; need CI gate that produces manifest + signature

3) Control: Deployment change approvals (canary gating) | SOC2: CC7 (change mgmt) | Owner: platform-engineering | Evidence: rollout dashboards + manual approval logs (pagerduty) | Confidence: medium-high | Note: automated rollback exists but approval audit trail is split across tools

4) Control: Production log retention & access logging | SOC2: CC8 (monitoring) | Owner: observability | Evidence: elk/cluster retention policy + S3 lifecycle | Confidence: medium | Note: searchable logs require index warm-up; make evidence exportable for audit window

5) Control: Privileged admin sessions (Bastion + session recording) | SOC2: CC6 | Owner: infra/sre | Evidence: bastion recordings in vault + session metadata | Confidence: low | Note: sampling is not deterministic — auditor will ask for consistent retention policy

Quick risk threads (how an incident travels):
- Compromised dev key -> CI pipeline -> unsigned model pushed -> consumer-facing degraded responses (data exfil risk).
  Controls to strengthen: artifact signing, CI key scoping, pipeline isolation.

Unresolved questions / assumptions:
- Which teams currently have documented SLA/ownership for evidence exports? (I think only infra + observability.)
- How often do we snapshot RBAC roles for org-level services? No scheduled snapshot exists; we rely on live queries. Auditor will want history.
- Are there any legacy services with hard-coded credentials in private repos? I remember a note from 2024 but need to chase.

Cheap experiments (low friction, high signal):
- Add a GitHub Actions step that publishes model manifest (sha + repo commit + build artifact link) to a signed S3 path (2–3 dev days).
- Create a one-click auditor export: a script that bundles last 90 days of deployment approvals + session recordings into a zip for review (1 week).
- Weekly snapshot job for IAM roles (CSV + who changed) pushed to secure bucket (3 days).

Meeting notes (2026-02-25 sync with Marta + Noah):
- Agreed to prioritize model provenance and privileged session recording evidence.
- Platform will prototype manifest publisher by March sprint end.
- Trust-ops to draft evidence export template for auditors — scope: 90-day window, deployment approvals, access logs.

Next actions (my personal TODOs):
- [ ] File JIRA ticket for model-manifest CI step (assign to amy/pm) — target: JIRA-TRUST-4521 (open placeholder)
- [ ] Draft evidence export template and share with infra/observability for feedback (due: 2026-03-10)
- [ ] Inventory services with long-lived keys (ask SRE to run a scan)
- [ ] Confirm bastion session retention policy and propose deterministic sampling or full retention

Notes to self: keep this doc lightweight. When we have concrete artifacts, move polished mapping into Confluence (linked above) and mark this notebook as capture-only. If I get pulled into sprint work, flag the three items above as priority for the SOC2 prep runbook.
